Based on the information provided, some key lessons learned related to radiators from coastal areas include:

1. **Zinc Diffusion Layer Thickness**: Radiators from coastal regions showed perforated tubes after approximately two years due to a thinner than required zinc diffusion layer on the tubes. This issue was identified when Talvik Alloys supplied tube stock with 4 g/m² zinc arc-spray instead of the specified 8 g/m², leading to premature consumption of the sacrificial layer.

2. **Specification Tightening**: To address this issue, the specification was tightened to 8-10 g/m² zinc, and incoming XRF measurements of zinc load on coils were implemented. Additionally, a SWAAT (acidified synthetic sea water) test was added to the Design Verification Plan & Review (DVP&R) process.

These changes aimed to prevent similar issues in future radiators from being produced in coastal markets.
